history.summary: Landed webhook-relay/ in DockerImages on phase/015-P1 (commit 51f6653): a stateless Go service that verifies GitHub's X-Hub-Signature-256 at the edge and fans each verified delivery out verbatim to argocd-server and the applicationset-controller concurrently, both-or-502, plus its Dockerfile (golang:1.26-bookworm builder into debian:bookworm-slim carrying only the binary and CA certificates), README, architecture.yaml and 4 test files covering R1-R6 against stub receivers. Gate green: cexec go go test ./... (also clean under -race and gofmt -l) and cexec iac ./scripts/arch-validate.py */architecture.yaml over all 23 files; kaniko --context webhook-relay --no-push builds and the root Jenkinsfile is untouched. Done-record appended under P1 and close-out S2 filed for the one thing left open: the architecture consumption edge toward the two receivers, which needs UUIDs only 009's ArgoCDDeploy producer can supply.

One blocking finding: the fan-out client follows HTTP redirects, so a receiver answering 303 makes the relay tell GitHub 200 for a delivery whose payload reached nothing, and a 307 replays the signed body cross-host — both witnessed against stub receivers, and both defeat R2's both-or-502, the property the plan says the design exists to protect. Everything else is sound: I re-ran the unverified gate myself (go test, -race, vet, gofmt, arch-validate over all 23 files, kaniko --no-push, all green) and confirmed the production HTTP path the suite never exercises. Three further findings are advisory, not fix work.

findings.summary: relay.go:70's bare http.Client follows redirects, so relay.go:193 scores the last hop: a 303 receiver yields GitHub 200 with the payload never delivered, and a cross-host 307 replays the signed body.
V14's constant-time clause is unpinned: replacing hmac.Equal with == in signature.go:36 leaves the entire suite green.
HEAD /healthz answers 200 and POST /api//webhook answers 307, contradicting V04's and README.md:75-76's 'every other method/path is refused'.
architecture.yaml:4, README.md:9-10 and Dockerfile:12-13 call the relay the estate's only internet-facing service; 21 services are public today.

history.summary: Blocking finding F4 witnessed and fixed: a new table test across 301/302/303/307/308 showed the relay answering GitHub 200 ("both receivers accepted") for a delivery no receiver processed and, on 307/308, replaying the signed payload to the Location host. The fan-out client's CheckRedirect now returns ErrUseLastResponse, so a 3xx is the leg's own answer and fails the delivery as `HTTP 3xx`; README's configuration section records the constraint for 009. Gate green: go test ./... (also -race -count=3), go vet, gofmt -l clean, arch-validate over all 23 files. F1-F3 are advisory and untouched.

Round 1's one blocking finding (F4, followed redirects) is fixed at the root: the fan-out client now returns http.ErrUseLastResponse, so a receiver's 3xx is that leg's own answer, the 502 names the real status, and no hop is taken — closing all three traces. The new test is non-vacuous (reverting the client to &http.Client{} fails all five redirect subtests) and pins production's construction path via relay.New. No new findings; the gate, which the dispatch recorded as unverified, is green here: go test, -race, vet, gofmt and arch-validate.

Every requirement and ruling the plan owes a phase is delivered by P1 and provable in the tree: R1-R6 and the Go/runtime-stage, endpoint-path, architecture.yaml, tests-out-of-CI, two-routes and signature-wire-format rulings all land in DockerImages' webhook-relay/, and V13's hand-off contract for 009 is in the README. The three things the plan does not deliver are the three it explicitly assigns elsewhere — R7/V08 to the run loop's own doc phase (which has not run yet; test_rounds is 0), R5's leaf half and the chart manifests to 009, and the architecture consumption edge to 009 as close-out S2 — so none is outstanding work this loop owes a phase. The two real leftovers, B1 (V14's constant-time clause has no test behind it, and no non-flaky Go test can pin it) and B2 (HEAD /healthz answers 200 and POST /api//webhook answers 307, against V04's 'every other method is refused'), are already filed with full accounts and cost the operator one word each, well under the price of an executor round, a review round and a consult. Under the mechanical-residue exception I fixed close-out B3 in this session and struck it: the false 'the estate's only internet-facing service' claim in architecture.yaml, README.md and the Dockerfile, comment and prose only, corrected to the authoritative design's narrower claim and committed to DockerImages main as 6e01ede with the arch-validate and go test gates re-run green.

Ran the slice-testing-strategy procedure for 015_webhook_relay: the dispatch's Ansible gate sweep (12 commands, all green) is established input and was not re-run; independently re-verified all 14 verification.json criteria by direct code read plus a fresh cexec go go test -race/gofmt/go vet and arch-validate.py pass over DockerImages/webhook-relay (all green, run this session, not borrowed from the phase's own gate). 13/14 verified; V08 (R7's argo-cd/ document-set edits) correctly ends 'owed to doc phase' — confirmed still open in decisions.md/design.md/phases.md, and the plan itself assigns R7 to the run loop's doc phase, which has not run yet. Pushed the slice's 3 DockerImages commits (first push) and confirmed live: Jenkins job DockerImages build #2485 started automatically off exactly those commits with no registration step and went SUCCESS, publishing registry:5000/webhook-relay:2485 and :latest — logged as close-out N1. No blocking findings: V04 and V14 carry known, already-filed advisory gaps (close-out B1 constant-time comparison untested, B2 two refusal-matrix edge shapes) that consult 1 already judged non-blocking; nothing new clears the generation bar. Nothing is deploy-owed to the operator from this slice — 009 owns the Deployment/Service/annotation that would make an operator apply meaningful. Committed verification.json and close-out.md (N1) to AnsibleSpecs (a60daa2).

R7 landed across the argo-cd/ set: O3 closes as D49 (one relay URL, Argo CD off the internet), design.md's webhook section describes the relay path and its contract, phases.md A.4 drops the self-contradicting 'expose argocd-server with homelab TLS; decide O3' bullet for an internal-UI bullet plus the relay deployment and A.5 gains 015's two live proof items, history.md carries why nginx mirror and the off-the-shelf relays lost, and D6/D22/D39 lose the clauses the fan-out falsified; AnsibleSpecs/README.md gains 015's pending entry (linked-bullet convention, so close-out moves it by hand as with 008) and repoints 009's link. DockerImages README's refusal table now states what the mux actually does (HEAD /healthz -> 200, non-canonical paths -> 307), re-probed against the shipped code, closing close-out B2's documentation half; close-out.md gained its summary, focus lines and S4 (pending slices still quote the pre-relay set). Homelab decisions.md, docs/runbooks/ and /work/Ansible needed nothing — no standing rule moved and no runbook names this behaviour; /work/Ansible has no commit for this slice. Gates green: cexec go go test -count=1 ./... and gofmt -l in webhook-relay/src, cexec iac ./scripts/arch-validate.py */architecture.yaml (23/23), and kc project lint/build/test in /work/Ansible — logged to doc_gate_r1.log. Committed on AnsibleSpecs main (files staged by name: cfb53ee) and DockerImages main (f78afee); NEITHER PUSHED — the DockerImages commit sits ahead of origin/main and needs the operator's push, since the driver only pushes the Ansible branch. Architecture-model nudge: the docker-images producer gained a new SoftwareProduct (webhook-relay), hand-authored and validating, but no consumption edge toward the two Argo receivers — Argo CD is modelled by no producer yet, so 009's ArgoCDDeploy is where that edge belongs (close-out S2); the Ansible model is untouched — no host, daemon or external identity moved.
